title.value: Image-Guided Brachytherapy for Rectal Cancer: Reviewing the Past Two Decades of Clinical Investigation
title.justification: The title aptly captures the focus of the paper, which is a review of the clinical investigations surrounding image-guided brachytherapy for rectal cancer over the past two decades.

extractions.description: The paper reviews the progress and clinical investigations of image-guided brachytherapy for rectal cancer over the last two decades. It discusses technological advancements, clinical trials, and the effectiveness of high-dose-rate endorectal brachytherapy (HDREBT) in improving treatment outcomes for rectal cancer, focusing on non-operative management strategies to minimize treatment-related side effects.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily focuses on advancements in medical treatment for rectal cancer and does not directly engage with eco-responsible AI or sustainability topics as defined by the given categories.
primary_category.quote: This manuscript summarizes two decades of technological evolution and progress in clinical studies to validate this treatment concept from the pre-operative setting to prevent tumor recurrence and, more recently, the introduction of the objective of cure without surgery.
